knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, tidy = TRUE)

In this R Markdown Document, I will be incorporating weight data from the GRLS physical exam dataset into my analysis of RDW and longevity.

```{r loadlib, results='hide', message=F, warning=F}
library(zoo)
library(magrittr)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(survival)
library(survminer)
library(rcompanion)
library(nlme)
library(here)
```

Let's start by importing and cleaning the data the same way we have for the other analyses.

```{r reading data}
demographic <- read.csv(here("GRLS_data/dog_profile.csv"))
labs <- read.csv(here("GRLS_data/clinical_labs.csv"))
physical <- read.csv(here("GRLS_data/exam_physical.csv"))

# We are only interested in RDW in the clinical labs (for now at least)
labs_rdw <- subset(labs, test_name == "RDW")

# Since we need to control for body size, we need to only use dogs with a weight listed
physical_weight <- subset(physical, complete.cases(weight))

# We're only interested in dogs for which demographic data, weight, and RDW are all available.
demographic %<>% subset(subject_id %in% physical_weight$subject_id & subject_id %in% labs_rdw$subject_id)
```

```{r  cleaning demographic data}
# Event type for censoring. TRUE = death, False = all other outcomes
demographic$event_type <- demographic$death_date != ""

# Reduce all event dates to a single column
demographic <- unite(demographic, withdrawn_date, inactive_date, death_date, sep = "") %>% rename(event_date = withdrawn_date)

# If no other event date, include date when data released.
# This would represent the last follow-up, since the demographic data is released with no embargo.
demographic$event_date %<>% sub(pattern = "^$", replacement = "2025-01")

# Convert to year-month date type to allow for numeric operations
demographic$birth_date %<>% as.yearmon()
demographic$event_date %<>% as.yearmon()
demographic[demographic$subject_id=="grlsR2FVJBB","event_date"] <- as.yearmon("2023-01") # fixing incorrect death date; see grls_init_expl

# Determine age at event (in years)
demographic$event_age <-demographic$event_date - demographic$birth_date

# Clean up, keep only relevant variables
demographic %<>% select(subject_id, sex_status, birth_date, event_date, event_age, event_type) %>%
  na.omit()
```

```{r cleaning weight and RDW}
# Remove all non-weight variables (and remove any incomplete entries)
physical_weight %<>% select(subject_id, record_date, weight) %>%
  rename(weight_date = record_date) %>%
  subset(weight_date != "") %>%
  na.omit()

# Convert to year-month date type
physical_weight$weight_date %<>% as.yearmon()

# Merge with demographic to determine age (in years) at record date
physical_weight %<>% merge(select(demographic, subject_id, birth_date, sex_status), by = "subject_id")
physical_weight$weight_age <- physical_weight$weight_date - physical_weight$birth_date
physical_weight$sex_status %<>% as.factor()

# Remove all non-RDW variables (and remove any incomplete entries)
labs_rdw %<>% select(subject_id, visit_date, test_value) %>%
  rename(RDW_date = visit_date, RDW = test_value) %>%
  subset(RDW_date != "")
labs_rdw$RDW %<>% as.numeric()
labs_rdw %<>% na.omit()

# Convert to year-month date type
labs_rdw$RDW_date %<>% as.yearmon()

# Merge with demographic to determine age (in years) at record date
labs_rdw %<>% merge(select(demographic, subject_id, birth_date, sex_status), by = "subject_id")
labs_rdw$RDW_age <- labs_rdw$RDW_date - labs_rdw$birth_date
labs_rdw$sex_status %<>% as.factor()
```

```{r RDW transform}
labs_rdw$RDW_Blom <- blom(labs_rdw$RDW) # Normal scores transformation on RDW
```

It will also be helpful to define a dataset with Percentage of Life Lived.

```{r Determining PLL}
# Create a new dataframe with only labs for dogs that aren't censored
labs_rdw_dead <- labs_rdw[labs_rdw$subject_id %in% demographic[which(demographic$event_type), "subject_id"],]

# Merge with demographic to get age at death
labs_rdw_dead %<>% merge(select(demographic, subject_id, event_age), by = "subject_id")

# Divide age at RDW by age at death to determine percentage of life lived at RDW
labs_rdw_dead$RDW_PLL <- labs_rdw_dead$RDW_age / labs_rdw_dead$event_age
```

Time points where weights are taken don't necessarily correspond to those where RDW is taken. Let's see how much they match up.

```{r Weight matches}
match_vec <- c()
for(dog in unique(labs_rdw$subject_id)) {
  match_vec %<>% c(
    labs_rdw[labs_rdw$subject_id == dog, "RDW_date"] %in%
        physical_weight[physical_weight$subject_id == dog, "weight_date"]
    )
}

print("Number of RDW entries with a corresponding weight:")
sum(match_vec, na.rm = TRUE)

print("Number of RDW entries with no corresponding weight:")
sum(!match_vec, na.rm = TRUE)
``` 

Not great. Let's see about performing a rolling join, so that previous weight measurements can carry forward into the next RDW measurement. Any more than one year starts to feel like the weight measurement will be unreliable, so that can be our cutoff.

```{r Weight Join}
rdw_weight_join <- inner_join( # Keep only rows with values in both tables
  labs_rdw, select(physical_weight, -birth_date, -sex_status),
  join_by(subject_id, closest(RDW_age >= weight_age)) # Rolling join, carry over last weight measurement
  ) %>% 
  subset(RDW_age - weight_age <= 1) # Pipe to subset and remove all weight measures >1 yr old

rdw_PLL_weight_join <- inner_join( # Keep only rows with values in both tables
  labs_rdw_dead, select(physical_weight, -birth_date, -sex_status),
  join_by(subject_id, closest(RDW_age >= weight_age)) # Rolling join, carry over last weight measurement
  ) %>% 
  subset(RDW_age - weight_age <= 1) # Pipe to subset and remove all weight measures >1 yr old

# Histogram to visualize the distribution of time between RDW and weight measures
hist(rdw_weight_join$RDW_age - rdw_weight_join$weight_age)
hist(rdw_PLL_weight_join$RDW_age - rdw_PLL_weight_join$weight_age)
```

```{r LMEs}
age_sex_weight_lme <- lme(RDW_Blom ~ RDW_age + sex_status + weight, random = ~ 1|subject_id, data = rdw_weight_join)
PLL_sex_weight_lme <- lme(RDW_Blom ~ RDW_PLL + sex_status + weight, random = ~ 1|subject_id, data = rdw_PLL_weight_join)

summary(age_sex_weight_lme)
summary(PLL_sex_weight_lme)
```

```{r Predicting PLL}
RDW_sex_weight_lme  <- lme(RDW_PLL ~ RDW_Blom + sex_status + weight, random = ~ 1|subject_id, data = rdw_PLL_weight_join)
summary(RDW_sex_weight_lme)

RDW_weight_lme  <- lme(RDW_PLL ~ RDW_Blom + weight, random = ~ 1|subject_id, data = rdw_PLL_weight_join)
summary(RDW_weight_lme)
```

Additions for plots/statistics from model

```{r}
library(performance)

# Calculate Nakagawa's R^2 for our model
model_performance(RDW_sex_weight_lme)

model_performance(RDW_weight_lme)

```

Predict PLL for late life only (where RDW shows sharp increase)

```{r}
labs_latelife <- subset(rdw_PLL_weight_join, RDW_PLL > 0.9)

latelife_lme  <- lme(RDW_PLL ~ RDW_Blom + weight, random = ~ 1|subject_id, data = labs_latelife)
latelife_sex_lme  <- lme(RDW_PLL ~ RDW_Blom + sex_status + weight, random = ~ 1|subject_id, data = labs_latelife)

summary(latelife_lme)
summary(latelife_sex_lme)

model_performance(latelife_lme)
model_performance(latelife_sex_lme)

```

```{r Plot RDW effect estimates}
rdw_effects <- effects::effect(term = "RDW_Blom", mod = RDW_weight_lme, quantiles = seq(0,1,by=0.00001))
rdw_effects_df <- as.data.frame(rdw_effects)
rdw_effects_df$high_int <- rdw_effects_df$upper + max(random.effects(RDW_weight_lme))
rdw_effects_df$low_int <- rdw_effects_df$lower + min(random.effects(RDW_weight_lme))

jitter <- position_jitter(width = 0.1, height = 0, seed = 1009)

ggplot() +
  geom_ribbon(data = rdw_effects_df, aes(x = RDW_Blom, ymin = low_int, ymax = high_int), alpha = 0.2, fill = "steelblue4") +
  geom_ribbon(data = rdw_effects_df, aes(x = RDW_Blom, ymin = upper, ymax = lower), alpha = 0.5, fill = "steelblue") +
  geom_point(data = rdw_PLL_weight_join, aes(y = RDW_PLL, x = RDW_Blom), alpha = 0.25, position = jitter) +
  geom_line(data = rdw_effects_df, aes(x = RDW_Blom, y = fit), color = "steelblue4") +
  labs(x = "RDW (normal scores transformed)", y = "Proportion of life lived")
```
